newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Vietnam ups '97/98 diesel, jet imports from Kuwait.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam ups '97/98 diesel, jet imports from Kuwait.

text.p: State-owned Vietnam National Petroleum Import-Export Corp (Petrolimex) has decided to hike diesel and jet fuel imports from Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) and extend its term contract to two years, sources said on Tuesday.

Petrolimex and KPC have agreed on the import volumes--about 700,000 tonnes a year for diesel from 500,000 tonnes in 1996, and about 120,000-130,000 tonnes for jet fuel from 80,000 tonnes previously, the trading sources told Reuters.
But the contract for oil product deliveries in 1997 and 1998 will only be sealed after the two parties agree on the price levels by the end of this week, they said.
The deal calls for diesel with a 1.0-percent sulphur content. The sources said KPC has requested for a three-year contract, with prices to be reviewed every year.
But Petrolimex preferred a two-year deal, with prices subject to six-monthly reviews.

Petrolimex also requested that a clause be included in the final contract to give the buyer the option to take diesel with a lower sulphur content of 0.5 percent, subject to changes in Vietnam's environmental regulations.
However, Petrolimex agreed to drop this condition when KPC agreed to a two-year deal.
The issue of when the contract can be reviewed will be decided along with the final price arrangement, the sources said.
Petrolimex forged its first long term contract in December last year for a one-year period. Under the 1996 agreement, the price was subject to review every six months.

Following the review of the 1996 contract in July, the diesel price was raised from parity to Singapore spot quotes to a 10-cent-per-barrel premium, on a free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis. Jet fuel was hiked from 10-cent to a 20-cent premium, fob.

Diesel prices on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Ho Chi Minh City were hiked to over 80-cent premium to Singapore spot quotes, from 70 cents previously, while c-and-f Danang diesel premiums were raised to around 95 cents, from 80 cents.
The sources said Petrolimex also held discussions with its other term supplier Marubeni International Petroleum Co (Mipco), a unit of Japan's Marubani Corp.
But chances of a contract renewal with Mipco were very slim due to a stand-off over prices, they said.
Petrolimex entered into a term deal with Mipco in March for the deliveries of 180,000-200,000 tonnes of diesel between April and December 1996.
